title: Bomber facing direction + ragdoll ground clamp

stories.title: Bombers rotate to face their movement direction
stories.summary: User reported: bombers never turn — when walking right the body still faces forward. New project-local system reads GridMover state per bomber: when mid-lerp (currentLerp > 0), face the (targetGx - gx, targetGz - gz) direction; else when queuedDirection is non-zero, face that; otherwise preserve previous yaw. Writes Transform.rotation.Y on the root entity. yaw = atan2(dx, -dz) so -Z is 0° (default Three.js forward) and +X is +90°. Skips dead bombers so the ragdoll arc isn't fought.
verification: acceptance: bombers face their movement direction. New project-local system writes Transform.rotation.Y on player.1 + bot.1 based on GridMover state. yaw = atan2(dx, -dz) (degrees) so +X = 90°, -Z = 0°. Mid-lerp priority via targetGx/Gz; queued direction fallback; preserves yaw when stationary. Dead bombers skipped.
examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: scheduler registers it after the animation driver
+9 unit tests covering pure helper + system (queued / mid-lerp / stationary / dead-skip)

stories.title: Ragdoll stops rotating when the root lands on the floor
stories.summary: User reported: 'the ragdoll lacks a floor collider — the bomber rotates around the attachment point on the floor'. Today death-animation-system clamps root Y >= baseY but keeps integrating angular velocity forever — the body parts swing through the ground in arcs. Fix: detect the landed state (root Y at base + vy <= 0) and (a) zero angular velocity, (b) clamp Transform.rotation.X + Z to [-90°, 90°] so the body doesn't continue past 'lying flat'. The bomber settles into a final tumble pose. Pure addition to the existing system — no new component.
verification: acceptance: ragdoll stops integrating once the bomber lands. When rawNextY <= baseY AND newVy <= 0 (landed): linear velocity zeroes; angular velocity zeroes; root Y snaps to baseY; rotation X + Z clamped to [-90°, 90°]. Bomber lies in a final tumble pose instead of swinging through the floor.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/death-animation-system.ts: clampDeg helper + landed-state branch in the integration loop
+1 unit test on the landed-state freeze

stories.title: Space press places OR detonates, never both on the same press
stories.summary: Follow-up to S104 KABOOM-REMOTE-DETONATE-SPACE-BIND. The S104 fix made Space fire BOTH PlaceBombRequest + RemoteDetonateRequest on the same edge — but bomb-fuse-system's trigger pass then detonates the bomb that was JUST placed this frame. User sees the bomb appear-and-instantly-disappear. Fix: in player-input-system, when Space fires, check whether the player has any paused bombs (fuseRemaining=Infinity) already in the world. If YES → emit RemoteDetonateRequest only (the player is detonating their chain); if NO → emit PlaceBombRequest only. F key still always fires detonate explicitly. Result: tap-tap-tap places 3 paused bombs (one per press, charges permitting), the 4th press detonates the chain.
verification: acceptance: Space fires PLACE OR DETONATE, never both. player-input-system reads BomberStats.activeBombs vs maxBombs on Space press: slot available → PlaceBombRequest only; slot full → RemoteDetonateRequest only. F key always fires explicit detonate. No more 'place + instantly detonate' single-press bug. Multi-charge chain placement still works (maxBombs=3 places 3 paused, 4th press detonates).
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/player-input-system.ts: SPACE_OR_PLACE_FALLBACK + REMOTE_DETONATE_EXPLICIT keysets, BOMBER_STATS import, conditional wantPlace/wantDetonate decision
Existing remote-detonate-pup tests still pass — F-only path unchanged

stories.title: Dead bombers ignore input (corpse can't steer mid-air)
stories.summary: Player-input-system was still writing GridMover.queuedDirection on dead bombers — the ragdoll arc kept logging keyboard updates. Fix: in the per-bomber loop, if BomberStats.alive === false → zero queued direction + skip all input writes (place/detonate/move). R-key restart still fires.
verification: acceptance: dead bombers no longer respond to input. Per-bomber loop short-circuits on alive=false: queuedDirection cleared, PLACE/DETONATE/MOVE skipped, R-key restart still fires.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/player-input-system.ts: alive-check guard at the top of the per-entity loop
+4 unit tests covering each input path

stories.title: Ragdoll stops at hard-block walls (grid-raycast, no Rapier)
stories.summary: User noted: 'will obstacles block them from flying over'. Current ragdoll is pure scalar math — no collision checks, the bomber could visually clip through walls. Add a simple per-fixedUpdate guard in death-animation-system: before writing nextPos, sample the destination cell via GridOccupancyQuery.blocked(gx, gz, 'blast'). If a hard-block sits there, zero the corresponding horizontal velocity axis (x or z) so the bomber stops along that direction but keeps falling. Cheap + project-local + no physics.
verification: acceptance: ragdoll stops along an axis when it hits a hard-block wall. death-animation-system samples destination cell per-axis via GridOccupancyQuery.blocked(gx, gz, 'blast'); zeros vx or vz when a hard-block sits there. Bomber still falls (Y axis untouched). No Rapier — pure cell raycast.
examples/kaboom-crew/src/systems/death-animation-system.ts: KaboomDeathAnimationSystemOptions gains optional occupancy; integration loop samples nextX/nextZ cells + zeroes velocity on block hits
examples/kaboom-crew/bootstrap.ts: createKaboomDeathAnimationSystem({ occupancy }) — shares the same occupancy handle the other systems use

stories.title: Bench preset selector — load game characters into the editor + export URL
stories.summary: User asked: in the character editor be able to pick which bomber is used in-game (player.1, bot.1, eventually any registered character) and edit + save its recipe. MVP this sprint: bench panel gets a 'Preset' dropdown listing { custom, player.1, bot.1 }. Picking a preset writes resolveRecipeFromSeed(name) into the bench state (every slider snaps to the preset's value); picking 'custom' is a no-op. A new 'Copy recipe URL' button below the dropdown serialises the current bench state to a base64 recipe via stateToRecipe → encodeRecipe and copies `?project=kaboom-crew&recipe=<encoded>` to the clipboard. That URL is the canonical export — paste it into Kaboom Crew to USE the edited bomber. Disk-write workflow (a dev-bridge /__agf/recipe/save endpoint that persists into kaboom-crew/recipes/<owner>.recipe.json) deferred to a follow-up sprint — clipboard URL unblocks the immediate iteration loop.
verification: acceptance: bench panel gains a 'Game recipe' section with a Preset dropdown ({custom, player.1, bot.1}) + a 'Copy recipe URL' button. Picking a preset writes resolveRecipeFromSeed(name) into the bench state and the panel sliders snap to the preset's values. Copy button serialises the current state via stateToRecipe → encodeRecipe to a base64 URL '?project=kaboom-crew&recipe=<encoded>' + writes to the clipboard (falls back to console.log when navigator.clipboard is unavailable).
examples/procbomber-bench/src/bench-ui.ts: buildPresetSelect + buildCopyRecipeUrlButton + flashLabel feedback helper. GAME_PRESETS table is easy to grow as more bombers register for the game.
Existing e2e smoke still passes; manual playtest covers the clipboard surface

notes: Both stories pulled directly from user live-test feedback after S107 merged. Small focused sprint.
